finiteTrace.fact: The failed group transition was STORAGE_RESET_BEFORE_REMOUNT, followed by openMode(compact, ro).
Compact open waits only for domcontentloaded, clicks the server-visible toggle immediately, and waits for the composer before calling the harness hydration check.
The product starts collapsed, and the panel/Assistant exists only when expanded or closing; expansion depends on the React onClick handler.
Once Assistant is mounted, the compact branch always contains the composer input.
The compact root is display:grid; no inspected compact style hides the composer.
The render contract proves collapsed markup has no panel and a hydrated click expands, mounts the panel, and focuses the message input.

findings.statement: The harness does not establish client hydration before its first compact-toggle interaction. Its only interaction-based hydration check runs after the composer that the interaction must mount.

A click on server-rendered collapsed markup before React attaches the toggle handler can leave the product collapsed and make the subsequent composer wait time out. LIVE7 retained no post-click state, so this mechanism cannot be attributed as the exact historical cause.

The sealed evidence does not show that the product reached expanded state, mounted the compact Assistant, or hid a mounted composer. Current source and render tests instead establish the expected post-hydration path.

The capture did not checkpoint compact toggle count/visibility, hydration readiness, widget state, aria-expanded, panel/compact-root/composer counts and visibility, URL, or cookie-region state around the click. The wrapper also allowed tee to mask the child failure status.

limits: No failure DOM, screenshot, broader UI state, exact child numeric exit status, or product exception was retained.
No actual browser, runtime, HTTP, Support, model, capacity, DB, or private-log observation was performed by this diagnosis.
The diagnosis cannot retroactively identify the exact LIVE7 UI state and cannot justify a product behavior patch.
Forgot-password destination remains unresolved and actionless.

requiredContracts: Establish a stable client-hydration readiness signal before the first compact toggle. If no stable public signal exists, add an observability-only SupportWidget readiness marker set in useEffect and a render test proving server-collapsed, hydrated-ready, one-click-expanded, panel-mounted, composer-visible, and focused states. Do not change Support behavior.

In a new append-only harness namespace, checkpoint fixed enums before click, immediately after click, and after the bounded transition wait: toggleCount/toggleVisible, hydrationReady, widgetState, ariaExpanded, panelCount/panelVisible, compactRootCount/compactRootVisible, composerCount/composerVisible, URL class, cookieRegionVisible, and categorized console counts. Serialize no page text, storage values, cookies, credentials, or private data.

Require exactly one toggle and the collapsed-to-expanded transition from one interaction. Emit predicate-specific fixed codes for missing/duplicate toggle, readiness timeout, no state transition, panel absence, compact-root absence, composer absence, and composer invisibility.
Checkpoint before and after every UI transition so an exception still leaves the last safe projection.
Preserve child numeric exit status. Do not invoke the child through an unguarded tee pipeline; use pipefail or capture logging inside the runner.
Keep the existing 54-row matrix, response oracles, request spacing, session accounting, privacy checks, and prior frozen evidence immutable.

assertions: one interaction changes collapsed to expanded in compact mode
panel, compact root, and composer are visible
language selection is deterministic after mount

review: Separate baseline review of the append-only BIND13 harness and any observability-only product marker.
Run no actual 54-row capture until the zero-request transition preflight passes in a new output namespace.
A later actual capture must use fresh capacity/readiness evidence and must not relabel LIVE7.
